summary: Router 0.42.6 closes TM-05's next action 'include tool results in the final-payload test' and, found while doing so, a gap in the credential scan (cloud.scan_secrets, used by request_block_reason when credential_scan is block, the default). cloud._texts read only message contents given as a string, prompt, system and embedding input. Traced B6: on the native chat path (/api/chat, OllamaShape) a message content given as a list of parts is forwarded unchanged by cloud._oa_messages to OpenAI-style providers (o['content'] = content), and assistant tool_calls' function.arguments go to every provider (OpenAI tool_calls, Anthropic tool_use input via parse_tool_args); neither was scanned (probe: scan_secrets returned None for a synthetic key in parts and in arguments as object and as JSON text). OpenAI- and Anthropic-format requests join text parts into strings in openai_api/anthropic_api before routing, so only the native path carried lists; tool call arguments came through every API. Now _texts also reads the text of dict parts with a string text and the arguments of each tool call (string as is, object or list as JSON text with ensure_ascii=False); malformed parts and calls are skipped, not errors (no exception path). memory.py's use of scan_secrets ({'prompt': ...}) is unchanged. Effect for operators: a request whose parts or tool-call history look like they carry a key now stays local (cloud tier skipped with the credential_scan reason) - a stricter default, noted as a possible behaviour change. B7/final payload: the new test runs proxy._Relay._via_cloud with the privacy exception on a body with memory facts, an assistant tool call, a Home Assistant live context (door sensor) and an unrecognised result; the provider receives the redacted copy (memory facts and tool result present, door sensor absent, unrecognised result unchanged per ADR-0125) and the client's body is unchanged; with unrecognised_tool_results keep_local nothing reaches the provider and the refusal is answered. Not scanned (unchanged): the client's tools definitions and format schema, which are forwarded to providers but are schemas, not conversation content.

findings.evidence: cloud._texts skipped list contents and tool_calls arguments; _oa_messages forwards list contents unchanged and both provider converters forward tool call arguments. A synthetic key there passed the credential scan (scan_secrets -> None) and would have reached a cloud provider. Pre-existing since the scan was introduced; found during this review, impact: the defence-in-depth scan against accidental secret egress missed agent tool-call histories and native content parts.
findings.resolution: _texts reads both; test_credential_scan_reads_every_text_a_provider_receives fails without the fix (3 of 4 places) and passes with it; malformed parts/calls are skipped.

tests.evidence: 8 tests OK. New: secret in a tool result, content parts, tool call arguments as object and as JSON text is found and the same bodies without it are clean (rejected case); instrument: _oa_messages forwards parts unchanged; malformed parts and calls skipped; final payload with memory and tool results through _via_cloud (redacted copy sent, door sensor removed, unrecognised result unchanged, client body unchanged) and keep_local (no provider call, refusal). With cloud.py from origin/main the scan test fails for content parts and both argument forms.

tests.command: every python test/... and tools/... command of all workflows in .github/workflows/, except run_tests.py and check_public_changes (run separately); plus ruff check . and router.py --check router/config.example.yaml --pure
tests.evidence: 93 commands, 0 failed (also after merging main); includes selftest_privacy_redactors (default corpus byte-identical), selftest_privacy_check, selftest_institutional_provider, selftest_security, check_control_flow.
run after staging this record; the test's key is the existing synthetic shape assembled at runtime.

limitations: The client's tools definitions and format schema are forwarded to providers and not scanned.
Secret patterns themselves are unchanged; a key format they do not know passes, as before.
No end-to-end no-egress test against a real provider; classifier quality remains TM-05's open action.

Re-reviewed after merging main with #197 (router 0.42.5, control UI styles, no overlap with cloud.py): the end-to-end suite ran before that merge on base 83a9fee; after it the workflow commands ran again.
